stem: A shallow pond and the sand beside it receive the same sunlight for an hour. The sand heats up by many degrees, but the pond water warms only slightly. Which statement best explains why the water changes temperature so little?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Water molecules are nonpolar, so they pass sunlight through without absorbing much of it and only a small fraction of the incoming heat is taken in by the pond.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Heat absorbed by the water is first used to break some of the many hydrogen bonds between polar water molecules, so less of it raises the molecules' motion and temperature.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cohesion pulls the water molecules together at the surface, which blocks heat from entering the pond.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Evaporation removes all of the absorbed heat immediately, so the pond cannot warm at all.

stem: A chemical analysis of an unknown biological polymer finds carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and phosphorus, but no sulfur. Which molecule is most consistent with this composition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A protein with many cysteine residues, because proteins contain nitrogen and sulfur.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A triglyceride, because fats are rich in carbon and hydrogen and store energy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A cellulose chain, because it is a large polymer built from many repeating subunits and its monomers are joined into long chains by covalent bonds.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A DNA strand, because nitrogen is in its nucleotide bases and phosphorus is in the phosphate groups of its backbone.

stem: A cell links 50 amino acids into one polypeptide chain by forming peptide bonds. Which statement correctly describes the water involved?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Forty-nine water molecules are released, one for each peptide bond formed by dehydration synthesis.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fifty water molecules are released, one for each amino acid added.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Forty-nine water molecules are consumed, because building a polymer requires adding water.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No water is involved, because peptide bonds form by simply joining two monomers directly, which makes dehydration synthesis seem to be a simple joining reaction.

stem: A potato plant stores glucose in its tubers as starch, while its cell walls contain cellulose, also a polymer of glucose. Which statement best explains why these two carbohydrates serve different functions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cellulose is built from a different monosaccharide than starch, so the two polymers cannot share a monomer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Carbohydrates function only as energy sources, so cellulose must be used as stored fuel like starch for the whole plant, including the cell walls.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The same glucose subunits are joined in different arrangements, with branched, accessible starch suited to storage and linear cellulose suited to rigid support.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Starch is a carbohydrate made by dehydration synthesis, while cellulose forms by hydrolysis, which gives it its different role.

stem: A scientist compares two fats at 4 degrees C. Every fatty acid in Fat 1 has only single carbon-carbon bonds. Every fatty acid in Fat 2 has two carbon-carbon double bonds. Which prediction is best supported by the structure of the fatty acids?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fat 2 is more likely to be solid, because double bonds are stronger and hold the molecules together.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fat 1 is more likely to be solid, because its straight chains pack tightly together.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both fats are equally likely to be solid, because both are made of carbon and hydrogen.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fat 2 is more likely to be solid, because it has more hydrogen atoms bonded to its carbons.

stem: One strand of a DNA segment is written 5'-ATGCCG-3'. Which is the sequence of the complementary DNA strand, written 5' to 3'?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 5'-TACGGC-3'

choices.label: B
choices.text: 5'-UACGGC-3'

choices.label: C
choices.text: 5'-GCCGTA-3'

choices.label: D
choices.text: 5'-CGGCAT-3'

stem: A reducing chemical breaks the disulfide bridges between cysteine side chains in a single-chain enzyme. The amino acid sequence is unchanged, but the enzyme loses its activity. Which level of protein structure is directly altered?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tertiary structure, because disulfide bridges between R groups help hold the polypeptide in its overall three-dimensional shape.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Primary structure, because breaking the bridges changes the order of amino acids so that the whole chain rearranges.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Secondary structure, because disulfide bridges are the main bonds in alpha helices.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Quaternary structure, because the bridges hold several polypeptide chains together.

stem: A white blood cell engulfs a bacterium into a vesicle and destroys it. Which organelle most directly carries out the destruction of the engulfed material?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Smooth ER, because it detoxifies harmful substances in the cell and keeps the cell safe from toxins that enter.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rough ER, because its ribosomes make proteins that attack the bacterium.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lysosome, because it fuses with the vesicle and its hydrolytic enzymes digest the contents.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mitochondrion, because it supplies the large amount of ATP needed for the response.

stem: Two cube-shaped cells are compared. Cell P has sides of 2 micrometers and Cell Q has sides of 4 micrometers. Which statement correctly compares their surface area-to-volume ratios?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both surface area and volume double, so the ratio is the same in both cells.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cell Q's surface area is 4 times greater and its volume is 8 times greater, so its ratio is half that of Cell P.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cell Q's surface area is 8 times greater and its volume is 4 times greater, so its ratio is twice that of Cell P.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cell Q's surface area increases 4-fold and volume 8-fold, so its ratio is higher because 8 is greater than 4.

stem: Phospholipids are placed in water and spontaneously form a closed bilayer sphere. Which description of the arrangement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The hydrophobic tails face the water on both surfaces, and the heads face each other in the middle so the water-loving side stays in the middle of the bilayer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All heads and tails mix evenly throughout the sphere because the molecules move freely.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The heads of the outer layer face the tails of the inner layer so the layers stick together.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The hydrophilic phosphate heads face the water on both the outer and inner surfaces, and the hydrophobic fatty-acid tails face each other inside the bilayer.

stem: A cell is in a solution containing equal amounts of four substances, and no transport proteins for any of them are present in the membrane. Which substance would cross the phospholipid bilayer most readily?

choices.label: A
choices.text: N2, because it is small and nonpolar and can dissolve in the hydrophobic interior of the bilayer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Na+, because it is a very small ion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glucose, because the cell constantly needs it for energy and the cell would take it in as quickly as it needs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: K+, because it is moving toward a region of the cell where potassium is abundant.

stem: The concentration of an ion is 140 mM inside a cell and 4 mM outside. A membrane protein moves the ion into the cell. Which statement best describes this movement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is passive transport, because a membrane protein is involved and proteins lower the energy needed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is facilitated diffusion, because ions are charged and charged particles always use channels.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is active transport, because the ion moves from low to high concentration, which requires energy input, typically from ATP.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is endocytosis, because transport against a gradient is always done in vesicles.

stem: Sodium ion concentration is 145 mM outside a neuron and 12 mM inside. Sodium channels in the membrane open. Which statement correctly describes what happens?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sodium ions flow out of the cell, because open channels pump ions out to keep the inside low.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sodium ions flow into the cell through the channels down their concentration gradient, with no direct ATP use.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sodium ions flow in, but only because ATP is used to power the channel, since a protein is involved.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sodium ions cannot cross at all, because charged ions are blocked by the membrane.

stem: A poison stops a nerve cell's ATP production but does not damage its membrane proteins. Which is the most direct consequence for the cell's Na+/K+ pumps and ion gradients?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nothing changes, because ion movement across membranes is entirely passive because pumps are not needed to hold ions at different levels across a membrane.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The pumps keep working at the same rate, because the proteins themselves are undamaged.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The pumps reverse direction and move Na+ in and K+ out by facilitated diffusion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The pumps stop moving Na+ out and K+ in against their gradients, so the gradients and membrane potential gradually dissipate.

stem: Lysosomes maintain an acidic interior and contain digestive enzymes. Which statement best explains the advantage of keeping these in a membrane-bound compartment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The membrane isolates the acidic conditions and digestive enzymes, so they do not interfere with or damage reactions elsewhere in the cell.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The membrane supplies extra ATP that makes the digestive enzymes work faster.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The membrane removes the need for any transport, since everything needed is already inside because the enzymes and acid are already contained inside.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enzymes cannot function at all unless they are surrounded by a membrane.

stem: Which observation most directly supports the hypothesis that mitochondria descended from free-living bacteria, rather than having always been made entirely from the host cell's own genes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mitochondria produce ATP, which prokaryotes also produce.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mitochondria are enclosed by membranes, like the nucleus and other organelles and so they must have originated as separate organisms from the host.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mitochondria contain their own circular DNA and ribosomes that resemble those of bacteria, and they divide in a way similar to binary fission.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mitochondria are found in almost every eukaryotic cell, which shows they are very ancient.

stem: An uncatalyzed reaction has an activation energy of 75 kJ/mol and releases 30 kJ/mol overall. An enzyme lowers the activation energy to 40 kJ/mol. What does the enzyme change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It supplies 35 kJ/mol of energy to the substrate so the reaction can start and then the substrate has enough energy to react without help.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It lowers the energy barrier to 40 kJ/mol, and the reaction still releases 30 kJ/mol overall.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It makes the reaction release 65 kJ/mol overall, because the barrier is 35 kJ/mol lower.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is used up in the reaction as it permanently joins the substrate.

stem: An enzyme has an optimum pH of 7. At pH 2 its activity falls to nearly zero. When the pH is returned to 7, its activity returns. Which statement best explains these results?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The acid broke the peptide bonds, permanently destroying the amino acid sequence.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The acid acted as a competitive inhibitor by binding permanently in the active site, and the pH change blocked substrate from fitting.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The enzyme ran out of substrate at pH 2, and fresh substrate appeared at pH 7.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Low pH disrupted hydrogen bonds and other interactions that hold the enzyme's shape, changing the active site, and the shape was restored when conditions returned to normal.

stem: The reaction glucose + phosphate to glucose-6-phosphate does not occur spontaneously. A cell couples it to ATP hydrolysis and the reaction proceeds. Why does coupling make the reaction possible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The energy released by ATP hydrolysis is used to drive the energy-requiring reaction, so the combined process can proceed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: ATP acts as an enzyme that lowers the activation energy of the glucose reaction.

choices.label: C
choices.text: ATP stores its energy in a form that is later released as heat, which speeds the reaction in the cell and gives the reaction an extra push forward.

choices.label: D
choices.text: ATP is simply energy itself, so it adds a quantity of energy to the glucose.

stem: Light strikes the thylakoid membranes of a chloroplast. Which pair of products of the light reactions is used in the stroma to build sugar?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Oxygen and glucose

choices.label: B
choices.text: Carbon dioxide and water

choices.label: C
choices.text: ATP and NADPH

choices.label: D
choices.text: NADH and FADH2

stem: When oxygen is removed from isolated mitochondria that are supplied with NADH, ATP production by ATP synthase quickly falls. Which statement best explains this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Oxygen binds directly to ADP and phosphate to form ATP.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oxygen is required to split glucose during glycolysis in the mitochondria in order to feed the later steps.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oxygen supplies the protons that are pumped across the inner mitochondrial membrane.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oxygen is the final electron acceptor, so without it electron flow stops and the proton gradient used by ATP synthase is no longer maintained.
